**The meaning of the verse**
﴿إِن تُبْدُوا الصَّدَقَاتِ فَنِعِمَّا هِيَ ۖ وَإِن تُخْفُوهَا وَتُؤْتُوهَا الْفُقَرَاءَ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ ۚ وَيُكَفِّرُ عَنكُم مِّن سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ﴾

If you give openly what you give in charity for Allah, how good is what you have given. And if you give it secretly and give it to the poor, that is better for you, because it is further from showing off; and in charity — with sincerity — your sins are wiped away. And Allah, who knows the finest details of things, from whom nothing of your circumstances is hidden, will repay everyone for their deeds.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. Why did Salman not give Ammar the money in front of the boys?
2. How did Salman answer when Bilal said, "I want to find out!"? And how did he answer when Ammar handed out the sweets?
3. Is giving charity in front of people forbidden? (No: ﴿إِن تُبْدُوا الصَّدَقَاتِ فَنِعِمَّا هِيَ﴾ (If you give charity openly, how good that is!). But giving in secret is better, especially if giving openly would embarrass the poor person.)

**This week's exercise**
Your child chooses a secret charity this week: money in a charity box, or a small gift with no name that they leave for a classmate in need. And they tell no one what they did — not even you.
